persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Jenny, 30, home for the weekend. Your grandfather, Joe, is 82. He keeps everything in his head: where the deed to the house is, which bank he uses, who his lawyer is. Today you sit with him and write it all down on one page, so the family will never have to search.

challenge.intro: Now you are Jenny, sitting with Grandpa Joe. The app is empty. Nobody will tell you which button to press. Use what you learned. Everything here is made up, so never type a real password. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Open The Key with the normal link (not the 🧪 test copy). If the welcome tour shows, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. Then scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap '🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data' → OK → OK (if it says 'There is nothing saved in this app yet', just tap OK: it is already empty). The top bar now says 'Nothing filled in yet — start anywhere.'

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: one page that tells the family where important things are kept
never the passwords, only where they are kept
print it and give a copy to someone you trust

lines: Welcome. This short video explains The Key: what it is for, and how to use it.
First, the problem. In many families, one person knows where everything is. Where the papers are. Which bank. Who to call.
If that person gets sick or passes away, the family can spend months searching. Papers get lost. Money is forgotten in an account. Photos stay locked inside a phone.
The Key fixes that. It is one page that tells your family where everything lives. You fill it in once, and you print it.
It is for anyone who wants to spare their family the hunt: older adults, and the children and grandchildren who help them.
One very important rule. The Key never holds passwords or PIN numbers. You only write where they are kept, like the red notebook in the desk.
At the top is a bar that shows how ready your Key is. It fills up as you add things, and tells you when it is ready to print.
Below are five sections. Tap a section's title to open it, or to fold it away. A tick shows the ones you have started.
Section one is My pictures live here: a phone, a computer, a cloud, or the albums in the closet. Tap Add a place your pictures live.
A panel slides up. Tap what kind it is, like Phone. Write which one exactly, and who can get in. Then tap Save, and your line shows in the section. Edit opens it again later.
Section two is My accounts that matter: email, bank, credit cards, subscriptions. There is a box for where your password list is kept. Write the place, never the password.
Section three is Important papers: a will, a trust, a deed, titles, insurance. Write where each paper is kept, and who has a copy.
Section four is The people who know things: the lawyer, the accountant, the doctor, the pastor. Add a name and a phone number. On an iPhone, you can fill one in from your contacts.
Section five is Anything else they should know. It is one open box for a wish, an instruction, or a kind word, in your own words.
Each section also has an Other notes box, for anything that does not fit a line.
Under the sections is a note on safety. It says the rule again: never write real passwords here.
Then comes the big button, Print my Key. You get a clean page with every section, dated today. If the page is empty, it asks you to write one line first.
Print two copies: one for a drawer at home, and one for the person you trust most.
There is nothing to save by hand. Every word saves on this device as you type, or when you tap Save.
Here is how to start. Open section one, and add one place your pictures live. Then open section three, and write where your will or insurance papers are. Even one line helps them someday.
When life changes, open it again, change a line, and print a fresh copy. The new date shows which page is the latest.
Everything stays on this device. There is no account, and nothing is sent anywhere.
The Key is free, forever. Daraja's profits help students in Kenya stay in school.
The round question mark button in the corner has the tour, help and settings, any time.
